clue.text: You can get bogged down in this pile of paper about company's meeting

definitions.text: You can get bogged down in this

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the paper pile is wrapped around the meeting

parts.note: a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper
AGM is the annual general meeting of a company

explanation.surface: Someone drowning in a heap of papers about a shareholders' meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A bog or marsh is a place where feet sink and stick, the literal sense of getting bogged down.

clue.text: The French who throw out a traitor

parts.note: qui is the French word for who
to sling is to throw or fling out

explanation.surface: French people who cast out one of their own betrayers.
explanation.walkthrough: Vidkun Quisling, the Norwegian collaborator, gave his name to any traitor who helps an occupier.
explanation.definitionFit: An eponym for a collaborator who betrays his country to an invader.

clue.text: Man burdened by tool briefly, a saw

indicators.note: briefly means the word for the tool is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: an axe is a cutting tool
IOM is the abbreviation for the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: A labourer weighed down by a tool, and it is only an old saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'burdened by' is a down-clue placing: the shortened tool sits on top of the island.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw in this sense is an old saying or maxim, a self-evident truth.

clue.text: Conventional place for white lines

definitions.meaning: moderate, avoiding extremes in politics or taste
painted white lines run down the centre of a carriageway

explanation.definitionFit: A moderate stance is likened to the centre of a carriageway, where the painted lines lie.

clue.text: Was furious about state being laid waste

indicators.note: about means placed around, so the anger word wraps the state

parts.note: raged means was furious
VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state

explanation.surface: Someone was furious about a country that had been laid waste.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravaged land is devastated or destroyed, the same as land laid waste.

clue.text: River's risen, back inside college grounds

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the river word

parts.note: the Cam is the river of Cambridge, here with its possessive S

indicators.note: back means the risen word is read in reverse

parts.note: risen means up

explanation.surface: The college river has flooded and come back into the grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the word for risen; 'inside' puts that within the possessive river. The Cam flows through Cambridge, a university town.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds and buildings of a university or college.

clue.text: Classic book — a scholar crams it desperately

indicators.note: desperately suggests frantic disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A student desperately cramming a classic novel before an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's 1843 novella about Scrooge is a classic of English literature.

clue.text: Confusing detail put into trite statement

indicators.note: confusing jumbles the letters into a new order

parts.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled detail inserted into a hackneyed remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A banal, overused remark is a commonplace: the synonym for a trite statement.

clue.text: Watch cutter go up and down

parts.note: to watch is to see
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Observe the blade moving up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move alternately upward and downward, like a playground teeter.

clue.text: Like Kipling's stories, put together very precisely

definitions.meaning: Kipling's ... Stories, tales of how animals got their features
arranged exactly right, neat and orderly

explanation.definitionFit: The Kipling title and the everyday idiom for something arranged exactly right.

clue.text: Epic poem from Virgil I adapted

indicators.note: from tells us the answer is drawn out of a run of the clue's letters

explanation.surface: An epic poem adapted from Virgil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' looks like an anagram signal, but the poem lies within VirgIL I ADapted.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Iliad is the epic of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Deign to give valuable tip to each of us, indiscriminately

indicators.note: a tip is the end or point, so the first letter of valuable is taken
indiscriminately means without order, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Graciously handing out a useful tip to all of us without distinction.
explanation.definitionFit: To vouchsafe is to grant something in a condescending manner, giving as a favour.

clue.text: Pale green first becomes the centre of public attention

indicators.note: first places the green word ahead of the pale word

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
light means pale in colour

explanation.surface: A pale green that suddenly becomes the focus of everyone's gaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Limelight was the stage lighting once used to illuminate the lead actor, hence public attention.

clue.text: Island's one business area

definitions.note: read as island is, the 's linking to the wordplay

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
biz is slang for business

explanation.surface: An island with a single business district.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibiza is a Spanish island in the Balearics.

clue.text: Where to find Rupert, down and out, ruined

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: anagram fodder, taken as written
anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Rupert has fallen on hard times: down, out and ruined.
explanation.walkthrough: Rupert Bear is a British children's comic-strip character who lives in the village of Nutwood.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutwood is the fictional English village home of Rupert Bear.

clue.text: Retailers have smartened, diversified

indicators.note: diversified means made varied, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Shopkeepers have spruced up their premises and widened their range.
explanation.definitionFit: Tradesmen are shopkeepers who sell goods, i.e. retailers.

clue.text: Choose not to participate in operation with unethical solicitor

parts.note: a tout is someone who touts for business pushily or improperly

explanation.surface: Declining to join an operation run by a crooked lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it means one who solicits custom.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to choose not to take part in an arrangement.

clue.text: Where to find kerbstones, in passing

definitions.meaning: kerbstones edge the road, so they lie beside the route

explanation.definitionFit: Literally at the roadside, and the idiom for an incidental remark.

clue.text: Continue to desire a hussy

parts.note: to want is to desire
on is an urging to carry on, as in go on

explanation.surface: A man keeps lusting after a woman of loose morals.
explanation.definitionFit: A wanton, as a noun, is a sexually immodest woman, an old word for a hussy.

clue.text: African member of order harbours a lot of prejudice

indicators.note: harbours means shelters within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a nun is a member of a religious order

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: bias means prejudice

explanation.surface: An African nun who holds rather a lot of prejudice.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nubian is a native of Nubia in north-east Africa, along the Nile.

clue.text: Support extremely heroic behaviour

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
very means extremely

explanation.surface: Backing someone exceptionally courageous.
explanation.definitionFit: Bravery is courage, the quality shown in heroic conduct.

clue.text: God said to be on the side of America

indicators.note: said to be signals a word that sounds like the wordplay

parts.note: a backer is someone on your side, followed by US for America

explanation.surface: A deity claimed to support the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, BACKER US sounds like the Roman god of wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Bacchus is the Roman god of wine and revelry.

clue.text: Work with almost simple style of architecture

parts.note: to go is to work or function, as a machine does

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is left off

parts.note: thick means simple or stupid

explanation.surface: A building project in a plain architectural manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Gothic is the medieval architectural style of pointed arches and ribbed vaults.

clue.text: Cattle are partial to the old kind of daisy

indicators.note: partial means incomplete, so the cattle word loses its last letter

parts.note: oxen are cattle
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: Cows that are fond of a kind of daisy from bygone days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' reads as fond of, but 'are partial' clips OXEN to OXE and 'to' joins on the old article.
explanation.definitionFit: The ox-eye is a large white daisy of meadows.

clue.text: Give support to clergy — but it's behind the scenes

definitions.note: a thing that hangs at the rear of a stage set

parts.note: to back is to support
the cloth means the clergy collectively

explanation.surface: Supporting the priesthood, though from behind the curtain.
explanation.definitionFit: A backcloth is the painted curtain hung at the back of a stage.

clue.text: Cat formerly seen around university

indicators.note: seen around means placed around the inner piece

parts.note: once means formerly

explanation.surface: A cat that used to be spotted round the campus.
explanation.definitionFit: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard, a big cat.

clue.text: Health practitioner in love, 17

parts.note: being in means being at home
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the answer to 17 down ends in a word for a route, read here as a track

explanation.surface: A doctor who has fallen in love with someone met in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: The number refers to the answer at 17 down; 'by' there serves only as a joiner, and the rest of that phrase means a route or track. 'in' means at home.
explanation.definitionFit: A homeopath practises an alternative medicine using highly diluted remedies.

clue.text: Frenchman and wife start all over again

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name

explanation.surface: A French husband and his wife make a fresh start.
explanation.definitionFit: To renew is to begin again or resume.

clue.text: Is a foreign lawyer able to represent this country?

parts.note: can means is able
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: Asking whether an overseas lawyer may act for this nation.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada is a country in North America.

clue.text: Spy resolved to make a difference in something demanding pluck

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
resolved means broken down and reworked, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to alter is to make a difference

explanation.surface: A secret agent determined to change things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resolved' rearranges the spy word, and 'in' sets the change word within it; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A psaltery is an ancient stringed instrument played by plucking.
